name: Gemcitabine + CISplatin + Durvalumab (TOPAZ-1)
disease: Biliary tract cancer (cholangiocarcinoma and gallbladder cancer)

biomarkers.note: The cisplatin/gemcitabine plus durvalumab regimen is NOT biomarker-restricted (no PD-L1 threshold required for the first-line indication). Biliary molecular targets - FGFR2 fusions, IDH1, HER2 (ERBB2), BRAF V600E, MSI-H/dMMR, NTRK fusions - are tested to guide targeted or immunotherapy options, chiefly in the subsequent-line setting, and do NOT gate this backbone. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Biliary Tract Cancers v1.2026, Principles of Systemic Therapy (BIL-C) and Targeted therapy (BIL-C 3 of 5).

lineOfTherapy: first-line for locally advanced, unresectable, or metastatic biliary tract cancer (category 1, Preferred)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: adequate renal function and fitness for cisplatin and hydration. If ineligible for cisplatin, carboplatin may be substituted.
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v1.2026, Principles of Systemic Therapy (BIL-C 2 of 5), footnote g (carboplatin substitution if cisplatin-ineligible)

drugs.name: Gemcitabine

provenance.locator: lines 114827 to 114828 (Ch. 37: gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 + cisplatin 25 mg/m2 IV days 1 and 8 every 21 days; the cytotoxic backbone shared with TOPAZ-1)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed. Ch. 37, lines 114827 to 114829. Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle. This is the UK-ABC-02 cytotoxic backbone that TOPAZ-1 combined with durvalumab; the gemcitabine/cisplatin dose is grounded, the durvalumab dose is not (see durvalumab drug entry).

drugs.name: CISplatin

provenance.locator: lines 114827 to 114828 (Ch. 37: cisplatin 25 mg/m2 IV days 1 and 8 every 21 days)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed. Ch. 37, lines 114827 to 114829. CISplatin 25 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle. ISMP tall-man (CISplatin). Requires pre- and post-hydration; monitor for nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and peripheral neuropathy. If cisplatin-ineligible, carboplatin may be substituted per NCCN BIL-C footnote g.

drugs.name: Durvalumab

provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy (BIL-C 2 of 5): Cisplatin/Gemcitabine + Durvalumab (category 1) Preferred; reference 5 (Oh, TOPAZ-1). Durvalumab per-mg dose and interval not printed.

drugs.notes: VERIFY: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Biliary Tract Cancers v1.2026 (BIL-C 2 of 5) establishes cisplatin/gemcitabine plus durvalumab (TOPAZ-1) as a category 1 preferred first-line regimen but does NOT print the durvalumab per-mg dose, unit, basis, or administration interval (given with chemotherapy and then as maintenance in TOPAZ-1). The provided sources (btc.txt; DeVita Ch. 37) do not print the durvalumab dose. It must be VERIFY-ed against a cited source; not inferred here.

regimen.cycles: gemcitabine/cisplatin backbone up to 8 cycles (maximum of 6 months per UK-ABC-02, DeVita lines 114828 to 114829); durvalumab schedule (given with chemotherapy then as maintenance per TOPAZ-1) is VERIFY.

premedications.name: Cisplatin hydration
premedications.notes: pre- and post-cisplatin IV hydration to prevent nephrotoxicity.

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: cisplatin is highly emetogenic; give guideline-tier antiemetic prophylaxis before each cisplatin dose.

supportiveCare: Antiemetics: cisplatin-based, high emetogenic risk on days 1 and 8; prophylaxis required.
Cisplatin hydration protocol; monitor renal function, magnesium, and electrolytes.
Immune-related adverse event monitoring for durvalumab (thyroid, hepatic, pulmonary, colitis, endocrinopathies).

monitoring: CBC before each dose (days 1 and 8) - myelosuppression
renal function, magnesium, and electrolytes before each cisplatin dose
peripheral neuropathy and hearing assessment - cisplatin
immune-related toxicity screen (TSH/free T4, LFTs, glucose, cortisol as indicated) during durvalumab

doseModificationRules.condition: myelosuppression or renal impairment on day 1 or day 8
doseModificationRules.text: Review required; hold or reduce chemotherapy per protocol for cytopenias or rising creatinine. Consider carboplatin substitution if cisplatin-ineligible. Physician decides.

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Hold durvalumab and manage with corticosteroids per immune-related adverse event guidance; obtain clinical review before rechallenge.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Ch. 37 Cancer of the Biliary Tree, lines 114827 to 114829 (UK-ABC-02 gemcitabine/cisplatin backbone doses shared with TOPAZ-1). Durvalumab dose not printed in Ch. 37.

guideline.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy (BIL-C 2 of 5): Cisplatin/Gemcitabine + Durvalumab (category 1) first-line Preferred for unresectable/metastatic disease (reference 5 Oh, TOPAZ-1); footnote g (carboplatin if cisplatin-ineligible). The guideline lists the regimen by name and prints no per-mg dose.

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for gemcitabine plus cisplatin plus durvalumab (TOPAZ-1) as first-line therapy for locally advanced, unresectable, or metastatic biliary tract cancer. Serves intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (#23), extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (#24), and gallbladder cancer (#25); diseaseId anchored to cholangiocarcinoma. The gemcitabine (1,000 mg/m2) and cisplatin (25 mg/m2) backbone doses on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle are grounded to DeVita 12th ed. Ch. 37 (lines 114827 to 114829, the UK-ABC-02 backbone TOPAZ-1 combined with durvalumab). The Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Biliary Tract Cancers v1.2026 (BIL-C 2 of 5) supply the category 1 preferred status but print no per-mg dose. The durvalumab per-mg dose, unit, basis, and schedule (given with chemotherapy then as maintenance in TOPAZ-1) are NOT established by the provided sources and are set to VERIFY; they must be VERIFY-ed against a cited source and were not inferred. ISMP tall-man applied (CISplatin), with cisplatin hydration and nephro/oto/neurotoxicity monitoring, plus durvalumab immune-related adverse event monitoring. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
